result.topic_en: Euler completes the solution of Problem IV by integrating algebraically, showing that both projections of the curve are conic sections, and then states Problem V: find a space curve maximizing or minimizing the integral of w(v) ds, where v is the distance from the origin.

ergo erit aequatio inter $x$ et $y$; at vero pro coordinata $z$

30. Commode autem hic evenit, ut hoc algebraice
expediri queat. Cum enim sit $p=\frac{g+f(u+2a)}{u-f}$, facta sub-
stitutione reperitur $\frac{\partial x}{x}=\frac{\partial u(u-f)}{g+2af+2fu-uu}$, cujus integrale
manifesto est: $lx=C-\frac{1}{2}l(g+2af+2fu-uu)$, unde
sumtis numeris erit $x\sqrt{g+2af+2fu-uu}=g$.
Denique si hic loco $u$ scribamus $\frac{y}{x}$, prodit ista aequatio:
$$gxx+2afxx-2fxy-yy=gg;$$
unde adeo patet hanc projectionem esse sectionem coni-
cam. Ac si hic loco $y$ scribamus $\frac{z-ax}{n}$, obtinetur aequa-
tio inter $x$ et $z$, pro altera projectione, quae ergo etiam
erit pro sectione conica. Hinc intelligitur hoc problema,
quod difficillimum videbatur, ad solutionem simplicissimam
esse perductum.

Problema V.

Posito $\sqrt{(xx+yy+zz)}=v$, si fuerit $w$ functio quae-
cunque ipsius $v$, invenire curvam per ternas coordina-
natas $x$, $y$ et $z$ definiendam, in qua haec formula
integralis: $\int w\sqrt{\partial x^2+\partial y^2+\partial z^2}$ maximum minimum-
ve valorem obtineat.

Mémoires de l'Acad. T. IV.                5

items.quote: Posito $\sqrt{(xx+yy+zz)}=v$, si fuerit $w$ functio quaecunque ipsius $v$, invenire curvam per ternas coordinanatas $x$, $y$ et $z$ definiendam, in qua haec formula integralis: $\int w\sqrt{\partial x^2+\partial y^2+\partial z^2}$ maximum minimumve valorem obtineat.
items.english: Setting v = sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + z^2), if w is any function of v, to find the curve, defined by the three coordinates x, y and z, for which the integral ∫ w sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2) attains a maximum or minimum value.
